title: Ops SLO Ecosystem — Cross-Functional Roadmap & Tactics
body:
Context and intent:

This is a working canvas for building an SLO-centric reliability program that spans product, serving runtime, infra, console, and CS. The goal is to move from ad-hoc service SLAs to a reproducible, measurable SLO ecosystem that: 1) ties to user impact (LLM inference requests), 2) gives clear ownerable signals, and 3) supports safe rollouts and automated fallbacks.

Why a distinct "ecosystem" framing?
- SLOs are not just metrics; they're inputs to routing, rollout, incident escalation, cost controls, and product-level communications.
- We need consistent SLI definitions across model variants, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, and across regions.
- This doc organizes cross-team touchpoints, experiment sprints, gating criteria, and short tactical playbooks for common failure modes (tail-latency, dropped streams, KV-cache misses).

High-level objectives (OKRs alignment):
- Reduce 99th-percentile end-to-end token generation latency for hosted-api by 30% for 512-token workloads in Q3.
- Establish SLO definitions and owner for the top 12 inference routes across product by end of Q3.
- Integrate SLO-based rollback triggers into the console rollout pipeline for canaries by end of Q4.

Audience: eng-serving-runtime, platform-engineering, observability, product-hosted-api, console-and-rollouts, customer-success.

Three-layer SLO model (proposal):
1) Surface SLOs (product-facing): success rate, user-perceived latency (time-to-first-token & time-to-last-token), structured-output fidelity (pass/fail on eval prompt sets).
2) Platform SLOs (service-level): RPC success rate, streaming disconnect rate, p99 tail latency service side, model-fallback rate, KV cache hit ratio.
3) Infra SLOs (infrastructure): GPU allocation churn, queueing time percentiles, instance preemption rate, node OOM events.

Key SLIs we propose to adopt (concrete definitions):
- E2E_TTFN_95: time from POST to first token (95th pct) for standard text-gen route (512 tokens).
- E2E_TTL_99: time from POST to last token (99th pct).
- STREAM_DISCONNECT_RATE: fraction of streaming sessions that terminate with client-visible error code >=500 before completion (1h window).
- KV_CACHE_HIT: fraction of requests that found complete prefix/KV entries.
- FALLBACK_RATE: fraction of requests handled by fallback model/region due to capacity SLOs.
- PER_TOKEN_COST_P50/P95: per-token compute cost bucketed by model family.

Owners and RACI (working list):
- Product SLO owner: Leah O'Connor (product-hosted-api) — owns customer-facing definitions, release comms.
- Platform SLO owner: Jonah Patel (serving-runtime) — SLIs collection, runtime instrumentation mappings.
- Infra SLO owner: Ethan Zhao (infrastructure) — node-level metrics, autoscaler configs.
- Observability & Alerting: Maria Gonzalez (observability) — dashboards, alert rules, retros.
- Runbooks & Escalation: Aisha Martinez (eng-sre) — incident playbooks, oncall training.

Cross-functional sprint plan (8-week, two-week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (wk1-2): discovery + mapping. Deliverables: canonical SLI definitions, data availability map (what's in metrics, logs, traces), list of gaps and owners.
- Sprint 1 (wk3-4): instrumentation & dashboards. Deliverables: dashboard templates for product/platform/infra SLOs, baseline data for top-6 routes.
- Sprint 2 (wk5-6): experiments & rollout policy prototype. Deliverables: canary rollback hooks based on SLO breaches, automated throttling/burst fallback prototype for highest-cost models.
- Sprint 3 (wk7-8): runbooks & run-the-first-incident. Deliverables: 3 runbooks (tail-latency, streaming disconnect, model-fallback), 1 cross-team tabletop incident rehearsal.

Gating criteria for rollout (what "good" looks like before turning on automation):
- SLO measurement coverage >=90% of top-12 routes (data + alerts firing in staging).
- False-positive rate on SLO alerts <5% over 2 week trial.
- Companion runbooks exist and owners are trained.

Tactical experiments (early ideas to prioritize):
- Prefix/KV cache warmup warm-path: simulate high KV miss load to identify breakpoints and safe TTL/refresh policies. (owner: Jonah)
- Streaming buffer backpressure: degrade chunk size vs latency to find minimal buffer for stable tail latencies. (owner: Platform)
- Model fallback health score: build composite health signal (latency + error rate + cost delta) to pick fallback targets automatically. (owner: Product + Serving)
- Synthetic user promptset probe: use small set of representative prompts to continuously monitor correctness/fidelity regression after rollouts. (owner: Observability)

Quick playbook snippets (notes-to-self style):
- Tail latency arrest: immediately drop batching window to 0s on surge, enable burst nodes for 10m, notify product and CS.
- Streaming disconnects: shift queueing to ephemeral autoscaled runners that favor small memory footprint binary. Force fallback to short-seq model when repeated disconnects occur >3% in 10m.
- KV-cache storm: detect >10% decrease in KV_CACHE_HIT over 5m -> trigger aggressive prefetch for top-1k prefixes + raise prewarm job priority.

Dashboards & alerts (minimum viable set):
- SLO Overview: trend lines for each SLO with burn rate heatmap and recent breaches.
- Route Drilldown: p50/p95/p99, errors, fallback-rate, kv-hit for each top route.
- Rollout Guard: canary p99 vs baseline p99, automated decision box (red/yellow/green).

Runbook excerpts (short):
- Incident: High tail-latency (>3x normal p99 for 10m):
  1) Triage: check queue length, batching settings, model changes in last 30m (who rolled).
  2) Quick mitigations: switch to fallback variant, reduce batching, scale burst pool.
  3) Postmortem: tag incident with SLO burn rate, run retrospective within 48h.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly 30-min SLO sync (eng-sre, serving-runtime, product, observability) — standing agenda: measurement gaps, upcoming rollouts, open experiments.
- Monthly reliability show-and-tell (30–45m) where teams demo dashboards and one recent incident learning.
- Quarterly all-hands on SLO posture and OKR alignment.

Risks and unresolved questions (open):
- How to map product-level notions of "quality" (structured output correctness) into a deterministic SLI we can measure at scale? (open: Maria + Leah)
- Cross-environment parity: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private have different telemetry — what subset of SLIs are portable? (open: Jonah + Ethan)
- Cost vs latency tradeoff policy: who gets final say when a fix raises unit cost by >10% but improves p99 by 25%? (propose: platform + product joint decision)

Immediate TODOs (next 2w):
- [Aisha] finalize canonical list of SLIs and share with teams (deadline: 2026-06-22).
- [Jonah] run quick KV-miss stress test against staging (deadline: 2026-06-25).
- [Maria] create initial dashboard templates and wire to synthetic probes (deadline: 2026-06-29).
- [Leah] curate top-12 routes by traffic & revenue impact (deadline: 2026-06-23).

Notes to self / rough fragments:
- Keep SLO names terse and machine-friendly; use dot-delimited convention: product.route.e2e.ttl.p99, platform.stream.disconnect.rate, infra.node.oom.rate.
- Consider a "policy library" on console for selecting SA (slo alert) thresholds per environment and tier.
- We should prototype a small SLA->SLO mapping page for CS so they can translate error budgets into customer communications.

Appendix: example SLO (concrete)
- Name: hosted.text-gen.standard.e2e_ttl.99
- Target: 99th percentile < 2.0s for 1-128 token completions, < 6.0s for 129-512 token completions.
- Window: 30d rolling, evaluation cadence: daily.
- Alert: burn rate >4x for 1h or absolute breach (p99 > threshold) for 15m -> P2 alert to SRE + Platform.

End of doc — this is intentionally a working artifact. Expect iterative updates; please leave comments in the doc or ping in #sre-reliability-thread.
